post.description: Internal, for offboarding and erasure; no caller yet. Removes every document, file, chunk and vector an Organization has, and, since ADR 0018, its Calls, Recordings, Transcripts, Moments, Deals and Deal imports (and the copy the transcription vendor holds of a Recording), soft-deleted ones included, without waiting for retention. Idempotent by end state: it answers 200 whenever nothing remains, and never answers 200 while data remains. A transient failure (the store, the vector index or the vendor is briefly unreachable) answers 503 server.unavailable with a Retry-After header, and a repeat with the same Idempotency-Key or without reaches 200 once the removal finishes; a failure that will not go away stays an error. Served on the internal network only; takes the Organization from the path.

post.description: Uploads one file (multipart/form-data, one part named "file") to the Organization's Playbook. Owner and Admin only; Managers and Reps get auth.forbidden. The type and size of the file part are checked before anything is stored: document.unsupported_type (415) and document.too_large (413); a malformed name or an empty file is request.invalid. The common request.too_large and request.unsupported_media_type apply to the whole request instead: a body over the envelope limit, or a body that is not multipart. Answers 201 with the new document in state "uploaded". If the content matches a document the Organization already has, answers 200 with that stored document, with its stored fileName (not the new upload's name), so a duplicate is an answer, not an error: a match on a "deleted" document restores it (state "processing"), and a match on a "failed" document re-queues it for processing and answers with state "uploaded". The page limit is not checked here: a document over it ends in state "failed" with failureReason "too_many_pages". Accepts an Idempotency-Key header.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a document: it is hidden at once and purged after the retention period, and can be restored until then. Owner and Admin only. Idempotent by end state: answers 200 with the document in state "deleted" and its purge time, and deleting an already deleted document answers the same. Takes no body.

200.description: The document, deleted.

post.description: Restores a soft-deleted document within the retention period; it is re-ingested from the kept file and shows as "processing". Owner and Admin only. Idempotent by end state: a document that is no longer deleted (restored by an earlier call, or never deleted) answers 200 with the document as it is. A deleted document whose purge time has passed but which the purge has not yet removed is document.not_restorable (410); once purged the record is gone and the answer is document.not_found (404). Takes no body.

200.description: The document, restored or as it already was.

get.description: Lists the Organization's Deals, newest first (sorted by createdAt, then id, the opaque Deal id, both descending), one cursor-paginated page at a time (at most 100). Owner and Admin only. outcome limits the list to one Outcome and appearedInImport=false lists the Deals that have Calls but never appeared in a CSV, so a mistyped deal id is visible.

200.description: One page of Deals, newest first.

post.description: Finds a Deal by the customer deal id, sent in the JSON body {"dealId":...} so it never appears in a URL, a query string or a cursor (trimmed, otherwise exact and case-sensitive). Answers 200 with the Deal, whose opaque id is then used in every path, or deal.not_found. Owner and Admin only. It changes nothing.

get.description: Reads one Deal by its opaque id (the deal_ id from a list or a lookup, never the customer deal id, which is found with the lookup route). Owner and Admin only. A Deal cannot be deleted on its own.

200.description: The Deal.

put.description: Sets or corrects a Deal's Outcome (won, lost or open), even a decided one. Owner and Admin only. Idempotent by end state. A change bumps the Deal's Outcome sequence and queues the re-tag of its Moments; search follows the database at once for a lost Deal and may lag for a Deal that has just become won.

200.description: The Deal, with its Outcome as set (unchanged for a repeat).

post.description: Uploads the fixed CSV template (columns deal_id, outcome, closed_at, amount, currency and optionally name; closed_at is a plain YYYY-MM-DD date, kept as written, and a value with a time or an offset is a rejected row with the reason invalid_closed_at; up to 10 MB and 50,000 rows) as multipart/form-data with one file part named "file". Owner and Admin only. The type, size and first row are checked before anything is stored: deal_import.unsupported_type (415), deal_import.too_large (413) and deal_import.header_invalid (422). An Organization with MAX_QUEUED_DEAL_IMPORTS (5) imports not yet finished (state uploaded or processing) is refused with deal_import.busy (429) and nothing is stored; the count is checked before the file is stored, so a refused upload leaves no import. The header is read with checkDealImportHeaderText (the same reader and limits as parseCsv) on the first 8192 characters of the file (a header still unfinished there is deferred to the job, not refused), and the job re-checks the header of its full parse with the same verdict. The rest of the file is parsed in the background job, never on the request path, under strict RFC 4180 quoting: a stray quote fails the file, and a cell over 1000 characters fails the whole file too (a cell up to 1000 characters is checked row by row, and a bad one is a rejected row); blank lines at the end of the file are ignored, and an interior blank line is a rejected row with the reason blank_row, so the report has no gap, and it still counts in the row numbers, and rowNumber is the record number with the header as record 1. Answers 202 with the import in state "uploaded"; it is processed in the background. Imports are not deduplicated by content: each upload is a new import, and only the Idempotency-Key makes a retry of the same request answer with the stored import. Valid rows are applied and bad rows are reported, never dropped: a deal id already won or lost, or repeated within the file, is a rejected row in the report, not an HTTP error. A file with more rows than the limit, a cell over the length limit or a quoting error ends in state "failed" with failureReason "too_many_rows" or "unreadable". Accepts an Idempotency-Key header.

post.description: Uploads one Call as a Transcript (txt, vtt, srt or json, up to 5 MB) or a Recording (mp3, m4a, wav, ogg, webm or flac, up to 500 MB, streamed to storage and never held whole), as multipart/form-data with one file part named "file" and the text fields "dealId" and "rep". Owner and Admin only; Managers and Reps get auth.forbidden. A Transcript needs "rep", the JSON {"by":"speaker","label":...}; a per-side Recording takes {"by":"channel","channel":"left"|"right"}; a Recording with no "rep" waits in state "awaiting_rep" after transcription until an Owner or Admin picks one. A Deal that does not exist yet is created "open". Refused with rights.confirmation_required (403, its details name the wording version to show) until the Organization has a current rights confirmation. The type and size of the file part are checked before anything is stored: call.unsupported_type (415) and call.too_large (413); a malformed name, an empty file or a bad field is request.invalid, and a Rep choice that does not suit the kind is call.rep_invalid. The common request.too_large and request.unsupported_media_type apply to the whole request instead. Answers 201 with the new Call in state "uploaded". If the content matches a Call the Organization already has under the same Deal, answers 200 with that stored Call: a match on a "deleted" Call restores it (state "processing") and a match on a "failed" Call under the same Deal whose failureReason is transcription_failed, transcription_timed_out or processing_failed (reasons that can be transient) re-queues it for processing (state "uploaded"); a match on a failed Call with any other reason answers 200 with the failed Call unchanged, because the same file would fail the same way: rep_label_not_found and not_per_side are fixed by changing the Rep, and too_many_speakers, no_turns, too_few_speakers, too_long and unreadable by choosing to delete the Call and upload a corrected file; any other match returns the Call as it is. The same content under another deal id is call.content_in_other_deal. A recording over 3 hours, a Transcript with no turns or fewer than two speakers, or a Rep label not in the file is not checked here: the Call ends in state "failed" with a failureReason. Accepts an Idempotency-Key header.
post.summary: Upload a Call Transcript or Recording

get.description: Lists the Organization's Calls, newest first (sorted by createdAt, then id, both descending), one cursor-paginated page at a time (at most 100). Owner and Admin only. Deleted Calls are left out unless state=deleted is asked for; state=awaiting_rep lists the Calls waiting for a Rep and dealRecordId (the opaque Deal id) limits the list to one Deal. A list item never carries speakers: only the single-Call read returns speaker excerpts.

200.description: One page of Calls, newest first.

get.description: Reads one Call and its state, with the failure reason when it failed, the speaker labels to pick a Rep from and the purge time when it was deleted. For a Recording with speaker labels, above all one awaiting its Rep, it also returns speakers: a short excerpt per label (the first turns of the speaker, at most 240 characters, cut at a word boundary with an ellipsis; at most 20 speakers) so a person can tell who is the Rep. The excerpts are tenant Transcript text: returned only to the Owner and Admin of the owning Organization and never logged. No other Transcript text or audio is returned. Owner and Admin only.

200.description: The Call.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a Call: it and its Moments are hidden from search at once and purged after 30 days, and it can be restored until then. Owner and Admin only. Idempotent by end state: answers 200 with the Call in state "deleted" and its purge time, and deleting an already deleted Call answers the same. Takes no body.

200.description: The Call in state deleted, with its purge time.

post.description: Restores a soft-deleted Call within the retention period; it is processed again from the kept Transcript (a Recording is never transcribed twice) and shows as "processing". Owner and Admin only. Idempotent by end state: a Call that is no longer deleted answers 200 with the Call as it is. A deleted Call whose purge time has passed but which the purge has not yet removed is call.not_restorable (410); once purged the record is gone and the answer is call.not_found (404). Takes no body.

200.description: The Call, processing again, or as it is when it was not deleted.

put.description: Picks the Rep of a Call waiting in "awaiting_rep", or changes the Rep of a "ready" Call or a "failed" Call whose failureReason is rep_label_not_found or not_per_side, with {"rep":{"by":"speaker","label":...}} or {"rep":{"by":"channel","channel":...}}. Owner and Admin only, and any of them may pick, not only the uploader. A choice that does not suit the Call, or a label that is not among its speakers, is call.rep_invalid; a Call in any other state or with any other failure reason is call.rep_not_changeable. A different Rep answers 200 with the Call in state "processing": its Moments are rebuilt by a queued job and the Call is out of search until it finishes. Idempotent by end state: choosing the Rep the Call already has changes nothing and answers 200 with the Call as it is.
put.summary: Pick or change the Rep of a Call

200.description: The Call, processing while its Moments are rebuilt, or as it is when the Rep is unchanged.

get.description: Reads the Organization's recorded confirmation that it may share Recordings and Transcripts, with who confirmed and when, the version of the wording they saw, the current wording version, optionally the text of that version (also in RIGHTS_WORDINGS) and whether the stored one is current. Owner and Admin only. Without a current confirmation, uploads of Calls are refused; existing Calls are kept and stay searchable.

200.description: The stored confirmation and whether it covers the current wording.

put.description: Records the confirmation, with the wording version the member was shown, which must be the current one (else rights.version_outdated, 409). Owner and Admin only. Who confirmed and when come from the token and the clock, never from the body. Idempotent by end state: confirming the current version again changes nothing. A lawyer is to check the wording before real customers use it.

200.description: The confirmation as stored.

post.description: Finds Moments in the Organization's won Deals that resemble the conversation so far, so the Copilot can show what worked. The body is the latest turns (1 to 6, each a role of rep or prospect and its text, at most 2000 characters in all) and an optional limit (1 to 20, default 5). It answers the best matches, best first, at most 20, each with the opaque callId and dealRecordId, the momentIndex (the 0-based number of the Moment within the Call, so a Citation can point at exactly this Moment), a score and two snippets of at most 512 characters (what the Prospect said and what the Rep said next), and evidence: the number of candidate Moments and the distinct won Deals among them. The evidence counts only the over-fetched candidate window (the best min(100, limit x 5) Moments by similarity, after the eligibility checks), not every won Deal in the Organization. There is no cursor: the result is a bounded top-k. Only Moments of Calls whose Deal is won and whose Call is in search are returned, and only from the caller's Organization. It never returns the customer's dealId, name or amount. The request and the snippets are tenant conversation text and are never logged. It only reads, so it takes no Idempotency-Key and a repeat is harmless. request.invalid (400) for a body outside the bounds; server.timeout (504) when it takes too long; server.unavailable (503) with a Retry-After header when the embedding model or the vector store cannot answer. Owner and Admin only, as for all sales history (the owner's decision of 2026-10-13); a Manager or a Rep gets auth.forbidden, because a Rep sees only their own conversations. The phase-2 Copilot calls this service-to-service, not with a Rep's token.
post.summary: Find similar Moments in won Deals

200.description: The best matches, best first, with the evidence.

post.description: Finds passages in the Organization's Playbook documents that resemble the conversation so far, so a Rep can see what the company's own material says. The body is the same as for the Moments search: the latest turns (1 to 6, each a role of rep or prospect and its text, at most 2000 characters in all) and an optional limit (1 to 20, default 5). It answers the best passages, best first, at most 20, one item per chunk, each with the documentId, the document's fileName (the Organization's own file name), the page (the 1-based page for a paginated format such as PDF, null for a format without pages such as TXT, MD or DOCX and anything else the parser reads as one page; the service decides by media type), a score and a snippet of at most 512 characters, and evidence: the number of candidate chunks that survive the staleness check and the distinct documents among them. The evidence counts only the over-fetched candidate window (the best min(100, limit x 5) chunks by similarity, after the staleness check), not every document in the Organization. The query is embedded with documentQueryText (the turns trimmed and joined by a newline, no role labels), because document chunks are embedded as plain text. There is no cursor: the result is a bounded top-k. Only chunks of documents that are ready and not replaced are returned, and only from the caller's Organization. The request and the snippets are the Organization's own conversation and sales text and are never logged. It only reads, so it takes no Idempotency-Key and a repeat is harmless. request.invalid (400) for a body outside the bounds; server.timeout (504) when it takes too long; server.unavailable (503) with a Retry-After header when the embedding model or the vector store cannot answer. Every role that reads the Playbook (Owner, Admin, Manager and Rep) may call it, because the text is the Organization's own sales material; any other is auth.forbidden. In this service `page` is set only for a PDF (by its file name extension); it is null for PPTX and every other format.
post.summary: Find similar passages in Playbook documents

200.description: The best passages, best first, with the evidence.

post.description: Resolves the Citations on a Draft back to the text they point at, so a Rep sees why a sentence was written. The body is refs: one to 20 references, each a Moment (callId, dealRecordId and an optional momentIndex, the 0-based number of the Moment within the Call) or a document page (documentId, page or null). When momentIndex is present, a Moment resolves to that Moment of the Call's current build, or to removed if the current build no longer has it; when it is absent, it resolves to the lowest-numbered Moment of the Call's current build. An item for a Moment echoes the momentIndex it resolved (or was asked for, when removed). It answers one item per reference, in request order. An item is state available, with the snippets of at most 512 characters (what the Prospect said and the Rep said next for a Moment; the file name and passage for a document), or state removed, with the ids only and no text, when the Call, Deal or document was deleted, is no longer searchable, never existed or belongs to another Organization; none of those is an error, so existence is not revealed. It never returns the customer's dealId, name or amount. The snippets are tenant text and are never logged. It only reads, so it takes no Idempotency-Key and a repeat is harmless. request.invalid (400) for a body outside the bounds; server.timeout (504) when it takes too long; server.unavailable (503) with a Retry-After header when the store cannot answer. Every role that reads the Playbook (Owner, Admin, Manager and Rep) may call it; any other is auth.forbidden.
post.summary: Resolve Citations to their current text

200.description: One item per reference, in request order: available with snippets, or removed.
